topicName: Controller Filters and Action Controller Parameters
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Controller Filters and Action Controller Parameters in Ruby on Rails"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Mastering ActionController in Ruby on Rails involves understanding how to manage request lifecycles with filters and how to securely handle incoming user data with strong parameters. This tutorial covers both concepts in depth."},{"order":3,"type":"heading","text":"Understanding Controller Filters"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Controller filters are methods that are run before, after, or around a controller action. They are commonly used for authentication, authorization, setting up common instance variables, or logging."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Types of Filters"},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"before_action: Runs before the controller action is executed. Can halt the request cycle."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"after_action: Runs after the controller action completes. Useful for logging or cleanup."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"around_action: Wraps the controller action execution, allowing code to run both before and after."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Implementing Filters"},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"class ArticlesController < ApplicationController
  before_action :authenticate_user!
  before_action :set_article, only: [:show, :edit, :update, :destroy]

  def show
    # @article is already set by the before_action filter
  end

  private

  def set_article
    @article = Article.find(params[:id])
  end
end"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can also use options like only and except to restrict filters to specific actions within the controller."},{"order":12,"type":"heading","text":"Action Controller Parameters (Strong Parameters)"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Action Controller Parameters provide a secure way to handle incoming form data by requiring developers to explicitly permit attributes that can be mass-assigned, protecting against malicious injection of unauthorized attributes."},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Using Require and Permit"},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"class ArticlesController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @article = Article.new(article_params)
    if @article.save
      redirect_to @article
    else
      render :new
    end
  end

  private

  def article_params
    params.require(:article).permit(:title, :body, :published_at)
  end
end"},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"params.require(:article): Ensures that the article key is present in the parameters hash, raising an ActionController::ParameterMissing error if it is not."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"params.permit(...): Specifies which attributes are allowed to be passed down to the model for mass assignment."},{"order":18,"type":"heading","text":"Handling Nested Parameters"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"When dealing with nested data structures, such as tags or comments associated with an article, you can pass arrays or hashes into the permit method."},{"order":20,"type":"code","text":"def article_params
  params.require(:article).permit(:title, :body, tags_attributes: [:id, :name, :_destroy])
end"},{"order":21,"type":"heading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"By combining controller filters for request lifecycle management and strong parameters for secure data handling, you can build robust, secure, and maintainable Ruby on Rails applications."}]
